sources.entry: Oh My Android - Native control panel for the Android Emulator on macOS with ~48 one-click actions, Layout Inspector in dp, and TalkBack audit.

summary.one_liner: A native macOS SwiftUI control panel that docks beside the Android Emulator (and works with real phones over adb) to toggle dark mode, font size, RTL, TalkBack and other test settings with one click.
summary.what_it_does: Provides an always-visible panel with nearly 50 test actions for Android devices, including dark mode, font and display size, language and locale (RTL and pseudo-locales), TalkBack, bold text, layout bounds, show taps, animations off, network speed, GPS, and simulated incoming calls and SMS. A Layout Inspector shows view sizes and gaps in dp for Compose and Views, can overlay a Figma PNG export, and runs a TalkBack order and touch-target audit (Shift+Cmd+A). A Data Inspector reads SharedPreferences and SQLite of debuggable apps via run-as, and actions cover clearing data, deep links, APK install and resetting permissions. The app also ships an MCP server (ohmyandroid-mcp, 18 tools) so AI coding agents can take dp screenshots, read the UI tree, tap, type and change device settings.
use_cases: Test an Android app in dark mode, large fonts or RTL without typing adb commands
Measure view sizes and spacing in dp while comparing against a Figma export
Audit screen-reader order and missing labels or small touch targets
Let an AI coding agent screenshot, tap and check an app on the emulator
Inspect SharedPreferences and SQLite data of a debug build
Simulate slow networks, GPS location, incoming calls or SMS on an emulator
how_to_run: Or download the signed, notarized zip from the GitHub Releases page and move Oh My Android.app to Applications
claude mcp add --scope user oh-my-android -- ohmyandroid-mcp (optional, for Claude Code)
Build from source: brew install xcodegen; xcodegen generate; open OhMyAndroid.xcodeproj
notable: Single always-visible panel for both emulators and physical phones, with toggles the Android Studio shortcuts lack (bold text, pseudo-locales, layout bounds, show taps, animations)
Layout Inspector measures in dp for any app, with an 8 dp grid, color picker and Figma design overlay
Built-in MCP server with read-only or full-control modes that AI agents can use
No telemetry, no analytics, no account; nothing polls and device changes come from adb track-devices
Free and open source under MIT
caveats: Requires macOS 26 Tahoe or later and Apple silicon; not available for Windows or Linux
Needs an existing Android SDK (from Android Studio or android-commandlinetools); it bundles no emulator or SDK
Emulator-only features (GPS, battery, calls, SMS, snapshots, network speed, screen recording) do not work on real phones
